body:
The SPA e2e suite began running on main pushes with #1557, and it intermittently
fails with a TRANSPORT error rather than an assertion:

    Error: apiRequestContext.post: socket hang up
      -> POST http://localhost:8083/api/v1/books/6/metadata
      at setBookTags (frontend/e2e/tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:74)

The server closed the connection mid-request. That is a finding about the app
under concurrency, not about the test.

Evidence it is nondeterministic rather than a broken spec:
- Within a SINGLE run, against the SAME image, three of the four visible failure
  marks are RETRIES of two specs and they PASS on retry; the run's own tally is
  "1 failed, 364 passed". A deterministic breakage does not pass on retry against
  an identical artifact. This is the load-bearing evidence.
- The failure is a socket-level error, not an assertion. Zero assertion failures
  in the run.
- Independently measured by another session as 364 passed / 3 flaky / 1 failed.

CORRECTION (same day): an earlier version of this finding cited "a later main push
(#1561) ran the identical suite green, steps=21" as evidence. THAT CITATION IS
WITHDRAWN — it does not attribute to #1561. On a main push the e2e leg tests the
:dev image, i.e. the PREVIOUS build:

    tests.yml  refs/tags/v* -> that tag's image, ELSE -> :dev
    tests.yml  "Overlay this PR's SPA bundle"  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'

The overlay that makes the suite describe the code under review runs on
pull_request ONLY, so a main-push run exercises neither the head commit's SPA nor
its API. The retry evidence above is unaffected, since it is a within-run
comparison against one image.

Why it matters beyond the suite: e2e on main is wired to auto-revert, whose
premise is "Test Suite failed on a main push => the head commit broke it". That
premise fails twice over — the lane is nondeterministic, AND the run does not test
the head commit at all. Innocent commits get reverted (seen: #1563, a docs-only
commit). #1564 contains the revert side; this is the cause underneath it.

Worth checking whether the drop is gevent worker exhaustion or a blocking call
under parallel requests — this deployment has NO monkey.patch_all(), so one
blocking call stalls the hub. If it is the app, real users hit it under concurrent
load and the suite is merely the first thing that noticed.
title: The server drops connections under parallel e2e load, failing tests transport-level
